There are advantages of changing oil, Oils generally degrade with time. The gears will slowly wear and chips will get in the fluid. It is best to have clean fluid. Also, with an automatic, the clutch will start to break up, contaminating the fluid. Often, the pieces clog up small holes which control the shifting. This tends to start happening about 150k. When clutch really starts to go, you will need the tranny rebuilt or replaced; however, changing the fluid & changing both the fluid and transmission fluid filter, should buy you some time. I had trouble with an automatic shifting. I changed the fluid, and it worked. I have since also changed the fluid and the filter.

I am not familiar with any downside of changing the fluid, except the cost, which is much less than a transmission repair. Elsewhere in this thread, someone blamed a transmission leak on new fluid. It might have been coincidence. Also, if the old fluid was working, it seems one could use an additive to prevent leaks.
